newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar "safe-haven" status under attack.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar "safe-haven" status under attack.

text.p: The Singapore dollar came under attack against the U.S. currency on Thursday morning as U.S. funds were seen testing its "safe-haven" status, dealers said.
"People think the Singapore dollar would not be attacked because of its safe-haven reputation. But these U.S. funds are testing this reputation," a dealer with a European bank told Reuters.
"All the Americans want to do is to test the various stops to see how low the Sing dollar would go. They want to see how the weak shorts will be triggered out," he said.
At 0245 GMT, the Singapore dollar was trading around 1.4322/32 to the dollar.
Dealers said the greenback rose against the local currency after a British party emerged to buy on behalf of some U.S. funds from 1.4310 onwards.
"The Americans were buying the dollar against the Sing since late New York last night and they are just continuing to test all the stops," a dealer with a U.S. bank said.
He said the first stop at 1.4320 was tested and triggered and now U.S. funds were looking to test the next resistance at 1.4330 and 1.4340.
Some dealers said the Singapore currency's "safe-haven" reputation is fairly vulnerable this time due to a weak stock market and an economy whose growth has slowed.

"Previously, the Singapore dollar, with the strong economy, was seen as a good buy every time something bad happens in the region. It's not so now. I would tend to be neutral on the Singapore dollar," said the dealer with the European bank.
Most regional currencies were battered on Wednesday after Thailand announced a managed float exchange rate system, where the baht value would be determined by market forces.
The Singapore dollar, however, held fairly steady around 1.43 to the U.S. dollar.
